title: Park and Ride in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **49 lots, 4,523 spaces, all of them free.** Berlin's park and ride network sits at 38 S-Bahn and U-Bahn stations, and not one of the 49 lots charges for parking. There are 3,247 bike spaces alongside them.

**More than half are already full.** The city's own survey puts 27 of the 49 lots over 90 per cent occupancy and only 7 under 75 per cent. The realistic capacity on a weekday morning is about 800 spaces, and no lot takes a booking.

**Aim for Pankow-Heinersdorf P1 first.** It is the biggest single lot in Berlin at 407 spaces, it was under 75 per cent full, and it is 17 minutes to Alexanderplatz. Springpfuhl P1 has 410 spaces and an 18 minute direct S7, but it is in the busier band.

**An AB ticket always covers it.** Every Berlin lot is in fare zone A or B, so you never need an ABC ticket if you park inside the city. A single is 4.00 euro, a 24 hour ticket 11.20, a small group day ticket for up to five people 35.30.

**The green sticker rule is the real trap.** The low-emission zone covers everything inside the S-Bahn Ring, driving or parking there without a green Umweltplakette costs 80 euro, and foreign-registered cars need one too. All 49 lots lie outside the zone, so park and ride keeps you legal.

**Coming from the A10? Stop earlier.** Brandenburg has 59 lots with about 10,730 spaces, more than twice everything inside Berlin, including 1,392 at Potsdam Hauptbahnhof and 719 at Hennigsdorf. Those need an ABC ticket at 5.00 euro a single.

**Two lots have a day they close.** Parchimer Allee P1 has no parking on Fridays from 08:00 to 20:00 because of the weekly market, and Friedrichshagen P1 is closed to parking on Sundays for the flea market.
